map_edits_required.section: §3.7 · The radioresistance reappraisal — 'The shape of the resolution'
map_edits_required.why: ⛔ THE LOAD-BEARING REVERSAL. This paragraph asserts that durable case responses 'cluster far above the standard prescription in biologically effective dose', which is the dose hypothesis. The two contradicting SERIES were then retrieved and their delivered doses compared: the series that found NO benefit delivered the wider and, at the top, higher BED at every α/β tested. The paragraph as written points a reader at a hypothesis the data refute.
map_edits_required.anchor: **The shape of the resolution.** The registries cannot see dose
map_edits_required.current_text:
**The shape of the resolution.** The registries cannot see dose, and both are open to confounding by
indication — RT goes to the big, deep, close-margin tumours. Meanwhile the durable case responses
cluster far above the standard prescription in biologically effective dose: HDR interstitial
brachytherapy at 30 Gy in 2 fractions controlled **three separate metastatic sites for 36–41 months**
in one patient (**PMID 35494187** **[API]**), against 50 Gy/25 fx as the conventional STS prescription.
⚠ All BED arithmetic here is *ours*, α/β = 10 assumed, and no author quoted it.
map_edits_required.proposed_text:
**The shape of the resolution — ⛔ TESTED 2026-08-07 AND REFUTED.** The premise that the registries "cannot see dose" is false of the largest one: Masunaga 2025 states its delivered doses in full, and MD Anderson's were recovered at secondary level. Their BED distributions overlap, and the **null** series delivered the wider range and the higher maximum at every α/β tested — so a dose account requires the null series to have out-dosed the positive one. The durable case responses do cluster at high BED, but every one of them is a **metastasis-directed** exposure, and dose per fraction is perfectly confounded with treatment setting across the whole EMC record, so that clustering identifies nothing. Arithmetic, sweep and provenance: [`emc-rt-bed-reappraisal.json`](../modalities/emc-rt-bed-reappraisal.json); reasoning: [emc-radioresistance-reappraisal.md](./emc-radioresistance-reappraisal.md).
⚠ *Superseded, retained: "The registries cannot see dose … the durable case responses cluster far above the standard prescription in biologically effective dose … All BED arithmetic here is ours, α/β = 10 assumed." The α/β = 10 assumption in particular is retired in favour of an explicit 1.5–10 sweep — a single assumed value is what made the BED argument unfalsifiable.*

map_edits_required.anchor: **Free next step.** A BED meta-regression over every published EMC radiotherapy exposure
map_edits_required.current_text:
**Free next step.** A BED meta-regression over every published EMC radiotherapy exposure with an
extractable dose, fraction size and local outcome — case reports included, because at this incidence
they *are* the dataset — fitting local control against BED with α/β free, plus a propensity/E-value
bias analysis of the registry result. **Nobody has an α/β estimate for EMC.**
map_edits_required.proposed_text: **Free next step — DONE, and the regression half of it CANNOT RUN.** The BED and bias analyses were executed on 2026-08-07 over every EMC radiotherapy exposure with an extractable dose, fraction size and local outcome, case reports included. The bias half returned a result: correcting the registry for the one confounder it measured itself moves its estimate **toward** the positive series, and the E-values are recorded. ⛔ The regression half is **not executable**: fitting α/β free requires exposures that differ in dose per fraction while being comparable otherwise, and in the EMC record fraction size is **perfectly separated** — conventional in every curative-intent primary-site exposure, hypofractionated in every metastasis-directed one, with zero within-setting contrast. **Nobody has an α/β estimate for EMC, and nobody can have one from published data.** One home: [`emc-rt-bed-reappraisal.json`](../modalities/emc-rt-bed-reappraisal.json). **What would change it:** a per-patient dose-and-outcome table from any EMC series, or one cohort in which fractionation varied within a setting.

map_edits_required.why: The stated falsifier conflates two separable claims and only one is fatal. The model shows the fitness cost cancels in the time-to-progression ratio, so 'resistance is not fitness-costed' is not what bites; 'resistance is not a tumour-cell trait' is, because it removes a state variable. Same conclusion, different mechanism — and the difference decides which measurement is worth making.
map_edits_required.anchor: **What would kill it, and it must be the paper's centrepiece rather than a limitations line:**
map_edits_required.current_text:
**What would kill it, and it must be the paper's centrepiece rather than a limitations line:**
anti-angiogenic resistance may not be fitness-costed, because **the drug's target is host endothelium,
not the tumour cell** — so resistance could be microenvironmental, and competitive suppression would
have nothing to work with.
map_edits_required.proposed_text:
**What would kill it — RESTATED 2026-08-07, because the modelling showed this sentence names the wrong mechanism.** It conflates two separable claims and only one is fatal. *(a)* "Resistance is not fitness-costed" — **not fatal**: in the two-population model the cost raises time to progression in both arms by about the same factor and cancels in the ratio, because competitive suppression operates through competition for space rather than a growth-rate differential. *(b)* "Resistance is microenvironmental, not a tumour-cell trait" — **fatal**, and for a different reason: it removes the model's second state variable, so there is no resistant population to suppress at any cost. The gain instead runs on the **initial resistant fraction**, which is the axis EMC's mutational quietness speaks to — so quietness cuts **FOR** the premise, not against it.
